name: FIPS 140-3 approved algorithms
edition: FIPS 140-3 approved security functions (Annex C / SP 800-140C), with FIPS 186-5 and SP 800-56A Rev. 3
reference: FIPS 140-3, whose approved security functions are the Annex C list (materialised by SP 800-140C); plus FIPS 186-5, SP 800-56A Rev. 3, SP 800-38D, FIPS 203 (ML-KEM)
summary: Only FIPS-approved security functions. Notably excludes ChaCha20-Poly1305 and UMAC, which have no NIST approval.
notes: The X25519 and Ed25519 cases differ and the lists below reflect that: FIPS 186-5 (February 2023) approves EdDSA, so ssh-ed25519 is permitted for signatures, but the X25519 key agreement scheme of RFC 7748 is not compliant with SP 800-56A Rev. 3, so curve25519-sha256 is not permitted for key exchange. Validated modules vary and some omit EdDSA entirely. FIPS 140-3 is about a validated cryptographic module, not only about algorithm names, so treat a pass here as necessary rather than sufficient and confirm against your module's security policy.

kex.reason: SP 800-56A Rev. 3 approves ECDH over the NIST curves and the safe-prime groups of RFC 3526 and RFC 7919 only. diffie-hellman-group-exchange-* negotiates an arbitrary modulus from /etc/ssh/moduli, which is not one of those groups, so it is excluded; ML-KEM is approved by FIPS 203.

host_key.reason: Approved signature algorithms are RSA and ECDSA (FIPS 186-5), plus EdDSA on modules that implement it.

cipher.reason: Only AES is approved, in any of its negotiated spellings including the RFC 5647 names. ChaCha20-Poly1305 has no FIPS approval.

mac.reason: Approved MACs are HMAC with an approved hash, and the GCM tag. UMAC is not approved.
